extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers and preclinical drug discovery researchers (medicinal chemists, pharmacologists, virologists)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and experimental standards for optimizing and selecting small-molecule PPxY/Nedd4 antiviral inhibitors (VLP/BiMC/live-virus assays, ADME/PK, safety, and in vivo mouse efficacy) to advance candidates toward IND-enabling studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: VLP functional potency
rubrics_metrics.description: Low nanomolar functional activity (<100 nM in VLP Marburg and Ebola cell assay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VLP budding assays (mVP40/eVP40) are the primary screen; percent of VLP after compound treatment is quantified relative to DMSO control (set at 100%) by Western blot/Image-J. Compounds should show dose-dependent, robust blockade of PPxY-dependent VLP egress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular target engagement (BiMC) potency
rubrics_metrics.description: Low nM target engagement (<500 nM, inhibition of Nedd4/VP40 PPxY binding in cellular BiMC assay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BiMC assay: co-express NYFP-Nedd4 + CYFP-mVP40, quantify fluorescent complementation using confocal microscopy (Leica Sp5-II) and MetaMorph/quantitative scoring. Use PPxY L-domain mVP40 mutant as negative control and DMSO as vehicle control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live virus inhibition (IC50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inhibition of live virus proliferation (IC50 <100 nM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live-virus egress/spread assays (BSL-2 models such as VSV-WT/VSV-M40 and authentic BSL-4 pathogens in collaboration) with non-linear regression analysis to derive IC50. Use confocal microscopy and virus titration assays to quantify effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity index (SI50) threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Selectivity index (SI50 = CC50/IC50) ≥ 10 in egress assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine CC50 in relevant cell lines (HeLa, primary human MDMs) by CellTiter-Glo or equivalent. Compounds with SI50 ≥10 are advanced to primary human macrophage testing and further in vivo evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cytotoxicity margin
rubrics_metrics.description: Little or no cytotoxicity in mammalian cell lines at 50-fold higher than minimum effective concentrations (i.e., minimal compound effects at 50× MEC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform MTT/CellTiter-Glo assays at ≥12 2-fold serial dilutions and multiple time points (24, 48, 72 hr). Use CC50 to compute selectivity index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal perturbation of Nedd4/ESCRT cellular functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal compound effects on other cellular Nedd4 activities and ESCRT-associated functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess global cellular ubiquitination profile by Western analysis using HA-tagged ubiquitin in treated HEK293T cells; measure total and surface expression levels of TfR1 and EGFR by immunofluorescence/confocal microscopy to detect alterations in trafficking/degradation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability in human liver microsomes / favorable microsomal stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stable in human liver microsomes (low clearance and long in vivo half-life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in vitro microsomal stability assays (human and mouse) as indicators of clearance; stable compounds prioritized. Also perform incubations to generate/identify metabolites (phase I/II).

rubrics_metrics.name: No or low CYP3A4 inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No inhibition of CYP 3A4 (lower probability of drug-drug interactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure CYP3A4 inhibition (IC50) — earlier data noted no inhibition up to 33 µM for some analogs. Use this as a filter to reduce DDI risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADME property windows for oral drugs (cLogD and tPSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Orally administered drugs must maintain good aqueous solubility by maintaining lipophilicity (cLog D) and topological polar surface area (tPSA) values: cLog D < 5 and tPSA < 120 Å2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in silico property calculations (ChemAxon, QikProp) to monitor cLogD, cLogP, tPSA and guide medicinal chemistry to balance potency and solubility/permeability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitable aqueous solubility and permeability
rubrics_metrics.description: Aqueous solubility and permeability must be acceptable; low solubility/stability in assay medium is detrimental to SAR development and formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess aqueous solubility and permeability in vitro; poor solubility may explain poor PK or formulation issues and should be optimized (e.g., prodrug strategies, water-soluble groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable in vivo PK profile in rodents
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect low to moderate clearance, moderate volume of distribution, moderate to long half-life and good oral bioavailability; suitable ADME/PK properties for once-a-day oral administration are desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PK in male and female mice (IV and PO), and later in rats and dogs for candidates. Assess sexes separately to account for biological variable. Move compounds with acceptable PK forward to in vivo efficacy studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP PK/ADME suitability for mouse studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable ADME and PK properties for IP administration in mice (for initial in vivo efficacy/toxicity experiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial mouse PK under IP dosing to determine exposure; compounds with poor plasma levels (e.g., due to low solubility/precipitation) may be deprioritized despite microsomal stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo tolerability in mice
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerability in mice at doses up to 20 mg/kg (twice daily for 10 days) with acceptable clinical signs and limited weight loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform dosing in BALB/c mice, monitor weight loss, clinical observations (hair coat, discharge, diarrhea, food intake/activity), and mortality. Clinical score ≥12 for an animal is terminal and triggers euthanasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-of-concept in vivo efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration of in vivo activity in a mouse model of Ebola or Marburg virus disease (protection/delay in mortality, reduced viremia, improved clinical scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mouse-adapted MARV model (challenge dose, dosing regimen specified), measure survival, weight loss, clinical score, serum viral load by plaque assay; statistical significance threshold p ≤ 0.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go/No-Go potency thresholds for preclinical candidate selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds to move forward should meet: inhibition of live virus proliferation (IC50 <100 nM); low nM (<100 nM) potency for VLP and BiMC comparable to leads; minimal effects on other Nedd4 activities; little/no cytotoxicity at 50× MEC; suitable ADME/PK for once-a-day oral dosing; in vivo activity under oral administration; composition of matter patent protection worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this consolidated Go/No-Go checklist to triage 2–3 candidates for IND-enabling studies. Patentability (composition of matter) is required for freedom-to-develop and commercialization prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening tree throughput and triage
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 10–15 compounds/year that meet initial activity and in silico property criteria will be evaluated in in vitro ADMET assays; 2–4 most advanced compounds will be taken forward for non-GLP safety assays and further PK evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the flow scheme (Fig. 8/13) — initial VLP/BiMC/live-virus screens, then in vitro ADMET (microsomal stability, plasma protein binding, CYP3A4 inhibition, solubility, permeability), then mouse PK, then non-GLP safety assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard in vitro ADMET panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Use microsomal stability, plasma protein binding, CYP3A4 inhibition, aqueous solubility, and permeability assessments as reliable early indicators of clearance, half-life, exposure variability, and formulation feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assays are performed by CROs (e.g., Alliance Pharma); acceptable values per standard drug property criteria (Fig. 13) are required to advance compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GLP safety assay package for lead candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: 2–4 best compounds will be evaluated in non-GLP safety assays including: IC50s for seven key liabilities (likely CYPs) to assess exposure variability/DDI risk; manual patch clamp hERG assay; Ames mutagenicity testing with/without metabolic activation; safety panel of 44 primary molecular targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reputable CROs (Cyprotex, Eurofins) to identify cardiac, genotoxic, and off-target safety liabilities prior to IND-enabling studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary human macrophage testing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds with SI50 ≥ 10 in egress assays should be tested in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs); determine IC95 in MDMs to design animal treatment regimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform assays from ≥6 donors (50:50 female:male), replicates in triplicate, and determine IC95 for dosing design. Expect similar outcome trends though magnitude may vary among donors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay controls and quantification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate positive and negative controls and standardized quantification methods: FC-4005 (acylurea) as positive control in VLP assays, DMSO vehicle control set to 100%, PPxY L-domain mVP40 mutants as negative controls; quantify by Western blot/Image-J, confocal microscopy and CellProfiler as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reproducibility across independent experiments, use non-linear regression (GraphPad) for CC50/IC50 determinations, and apply consistent imaging and counting (e.g., ~100 images per condition for BiMC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Student t-test for two-group comparisons or one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s test for >2 groups with p ≤ 0.05 considered significant; inspect normality and use transformations or non-parametric tests if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform ≥3 independent experiments in triplicate where possible; report how deviations from normality were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex as a biological variable in PK and in vivo studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PK properties and in vivo responses in male and female animals separately to determine whether sex is a biological variable; if no difference, include both sexes in later studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sex-specific PK parameters (IV and PO) and consider sex when designing efficacy/tolerability studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of routing/criteria for moving scaffolds and analog strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue multiple medicinal chemistry approaches (stereospecific enantiomers, quaternary methylene analogs, water-soluble prodrugs, appended water-soluble groups/pyridyls, new scaffolds) and advance analogs that meet potency and ADMET criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative SAR guided by in silico properties, synthetic feasibility (FCCDC capacity), and empirical assay results; scale-up of promising analogs for non-GLP and in vivo experiments.
